briefs.headline: India inflation breaches 6% as foreign-led rally pauses; MSCI rebalancing and Hormuz risk complicate sector leadership
briefs.executiveSummary: Material PM change versus morning: Reuters reports October India CPI 6.09% (food 8.94%), breaching RBI upper tolerance band and increasing rate-sensitive downside risk. NIFTY closed +0.18% at 25,299.35; financials outperformed while autos declined. MSCI announced index additions/removal effective 30 Nov, a possible passive-flow event not observed buying. October AMFI equity fund subscriptions stayed positive but fell 13.9% MoM. Reuters reported Brent near $92.22 intraday amid persistent Hormuz shipping risks. Prior 11 Nov NSE-derived FII/DII turnover remains the latest independently retrievable gross transaction table; 12 Nov figures and primary NSDL sector allocations are unavailable. The repository's 14:10 IST automated snapshots are older than today's India close. Sector leadership and priced event-risk: as of 11 Nov private banks 3m +9.26%, +5.91pp vs NIFTY 50; pharma +7.53%, +4.18pp; autos -2.86%, -6.21pp. At 12 Nov 08:39 UTC Polymarket Dec Fed +25bp YES was 86.5¢ (+1.0pp versus stored previous snapshot; 24h betting volume $208,160; liquidity $788,374); Iran invasion before 2027 YES 7.5¢ (+1.0pp; 24h volume $239,870; liquidity $351,160). These quotes are not probabilities, policy forecasts, equity cash flows or evidence of today's later CPI repricing.

stories.title: October CPI 6.09% breaches RBI upper tolerance band
stories.whatHappened: On 12 Nov Reuters reported October CPI 6.09% YoY versus September 5.54%, above the 5.93% poll; food inflation 8.94%. MoSPI original PDF not independently downloaded in this review.
whyItMatters: Higher food prices pressure discretionary spending and may increase wage/operating cost pressure.
Inflation above 6% raises the probability of tighter RBI policy, increasing discount rates and funding costs; this is a scenario, not a policy decision.
stories.smartMoney: Not measured for this event; price action is not transaction-level institutional evidence.
stories.direct: Consumer staples, consumer discretionary, rate-sensitive NBFCs, housing and banks
stories.proxies: Food supply chain, agri-inputs, logistics, packaging; fixed-income duration
stories.whatCouldChange: RBI reaction, food-price trajectory, 10-year G-sec yields, credit spreads, NIM and retail volume
stories.caution: Some syndicated snippets disagree (6.9% typo); Reuters and multiple data sources consistently report 6.09%. Verify original MoSPI release and future revisions; lower crude may offset food pressure.

stories.title: Crude eases while Hormuz shipping threat persists
stories.whatHappened: Reuters 12 Nov intraday Brent $92.22 (-0.58%) and WTI $85.86 (-0.77%); Iran reported naval-mine damage to two tankers, with shipping incidents and unresolved regional conflict. Prices are timestamped intraday, not settlement.

Maritime insurance, rerouting and physical supply disruption can negate spot-price relief; geopolitical escalation may lift FX and inflation risk premia.

briefs.headline: Foreign capital is rotating toward India, but sector positioning and the global risk backdrop are not uniformly bullish
briefs.executiveSummary: The clearest verified shift is renewed foreign institutional buying in India's broad equity market after October withdrawals. Indian bank and auto stocks led price gains, although the latest fortnightly published FPI-sector data showed prior investment interest in IT/telecom rather than confirmed November financial-sector inflows. Oil-price moderation helps some importers, but shipping/geopolitical and monetary-policy risks remain. A global AI capex/valuation debate adds potential rotation pressure without proving an AI downturn.
